findings.root_cause: calculate() adds every supplied number and never rejects a mark below 0 or above 100, so -5 or 150 still changes the grade.
findings.student_explanation: a mark of -5 or 150 is still treated as a real mark.

findings.root_cause: the percentage divides by len(marks). An empty list makes that length zero and the program crashes.
findings.student_explanation: calculating with no marks crashes the program.

findings.root_cause: deposit() adds the amount even when it is negative, which removes money.
findings.student_explanation: a negative deposit takes money out.

findings.root_cause: withdraw() subtracts without checking the balance, so the account can go negative.
findings.student_explanation: you can take out more money than the account holds.

findings.root_cause: the username is pasted into the SQL text, so a quote can change the query.
findings.student_explanation: a tricky username can log in without the password.

findings.root_cause: the loop uses every index and also reads the next item, which does not exist at the end.
findings.student_explanation: the program looks one step past the last number and crashes.

findings.root_cause: mean() divides by the length of the list and crashes when the list is empty.
findings.student_explanation: the average of no numbers crashes.

findings.root_cause: ratio() divides by whole and does not stop a caller from passing 0.
findings.student_explanation: dividing by zero crashes this function.

findings.root_cause: the API key is a string in the file, so anyone with the code has the key.
findings.student_explanation: the key is written in the file instead of being kept outside it.

findings.root_cause: the database password is hardcoded next to the API key.
findings.student_explanation: the password is sitting in the source.

findings.root_cause: the default list is created once and reused, so a later call sees the earlier item.
findings.student_explanation: the basket is shared. The next call still has the previous item.

findings.root_cause: the loop starts at 1, so the quantity on the first row is never added. This one is less certain because some loops skip a header on purpose.
findings.student_explanation: the first row is left out of the total. A person should confirm that was not deliberate.
